# Tenklo Docs

> Tenklo is the integration layer for AI-built, code-owned product integrations. These files are curated for agents: core docs are listed directly, while provider-specific API pages live in a compact catalog.

Full core-docs context: https://tenklo.dev/docs/llms-full.txt
API and integration catalog: https://tenklo.dev/docs/api-catalog.txt

Use provider URLs by replacing `{slug}` with a slug from the API catalog:
- Main provider page: https://tenklo.dev/docs/integrations/all/{slug}.md or https://tenklo.dev/docs/api-integrations/{slug}.md
- Connect guide when available: https://tenklo.dev/docs/integrations/all/{slug}/connect.md or https://tenklo.dev/docs/api-integrations/{slug}/connect.md

## Getting started

- [Introduction](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/intro-to-nango.md): Build product integrations with AI, using code you control and infrastructure built for scale.
- [Quickstart](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/quickstart.md): Authorize an API and run your first Tenklo function
- [Coding agent setup](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/coding-agent-setup.md): Connect your coding agent to Tenklo
- [Use cases: Tool calling for AI agents](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/tool-calling.md): Give agents scoped, observable access to external APIs through Tenklo action functions.
- [Use cases: Sync external API data](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/syncs.md): Keep external API data fresh for your product, RAG pipeline, or change-detection workflow.
- [Use cases: Run external API operations](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/actions.md): Use Tenklo functions to read, write, and automate external APIs on demand.
- [Use cases: Process external webhooks](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/webhooks-from-external-apis.md): Receive provider webhooks through Tenklo, then forward or process them with functions.
- [Use cases: Build a unified API](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/unified-apis.md): Normalize several external APIs behind your own stable product interface.
- [Use cases: Customize per customer](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/customer-configuration.md): Adapt integration behavior for each customer without forking code.
- [Use cases: React to connection lifecycle events](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/implement-event-handler.md): Run integration logic when a connection is validated, created, or deleted.
- [Use cases: Sample app](https://tenklo.dev/docs/getting-started/use-cases/sample-app.md): A practical demonstration of integrating Tenklo in your codebase.

## Guides

- [Auth: Auth guide](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/auth/auth-guide.md): Let your users connect external APIs to your agents & apps.
- [Auth: Share a connect link](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/auth/share-connect-link.md): Generate a short-lived connect link and share it with your end user.
- [Auth: Connection tags, configuration, and metadata](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/auth/connection-tags-configuration-metadata.md): Use tags, connection configuration, and metadata for the right connection-level data.
- [Auth: Customize Connect UI](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/auth/customize-connect-ui.md): Guide to branding Tenklo Connect UI, overriding setup links, or building a headless auth flow with your own UI.
- [Auth: Token refreshing & validity](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/auth/token-refreshing.md): How Tenklo handles OAuth token refresh and what to do when tokens are revoked.
- [Auth: MCP Auth](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/auth/mcp-auth.md): Let your users connect to MCP servers through Tenklo
- [Agent sessions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/agent-sessions.md): Optimized interface for AI agents to use integrations
- [Functions: Functions guide](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/functions-guide.md): Understand Tenklo Functions and choose the right way to start using them.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Sync function guide](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/sync-functions.md): Build sync functions that keep external API data fresh and consumable by your app.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Sync efficiency](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/sync-efficiency.md): Build sync functions that replicate external datasets without wasting API calls, memory, or compute.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Checkpoints](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/checkpoints.md): Save progress mid-run, resume after failures, and turn full syncs into incremental ones.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Records cache](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/records-cache.md): How Tenklo stores synced records, detects changes, and lets your app fetch deltas via cursors.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Deletion detection](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/deletion-detection.md): Surface deletes from the external API — even when the API itself doesn't expose them cleanly.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Real-time syncs with webhooks](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/realtime-syncs.md): Combine webhooks from external APIs with periodic polling for a reliable, real-time stream of changes.
- [Functions: Sync functions: Sync partitioning](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/syncs/sync-partitioning.md): Spawn multiple independent sync processes inside a single connection — one per mailbox, drive folder, Slack channel, repo, or any other partition.
- [Functions: Action functions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/action-functions.md): Build Action functions that your app, backend jobs, or agents can call on demand.
- [Functions: Webhook functions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/webhook-functions.md): Process external API webhooks inside Tenklo functions.
- [Functions: Event functions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/event-functions.md): Run function logic automatically when Tenklo connection lifecycle events happen.
- [Functions: Storage](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/storage.md): Use connection metadata as the default storage for function parameters and per-customer configuration.
- [Functions: Function logging](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/logging.md): Use function logs for local debugging, cloud observability, and production troubleshooting.
- [Functions: Rate limits](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/rate-limits.md): Guide on how to handle API rate limits from external APIs.
- [Functions: Data validation](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/data-validation.md): How to validate data in your functions and in your app
- [Functions: Testing integrations](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/testing.md): How to test your Tenklo integrations using dry runs, mocks, and snapshots
- [Functions: CI/CD for Tenklo Functions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/ci-cd.md): How to integrate Tenklo Function deployments into your CI/CD pipeline.
- [Functions: Unified APIs with functions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/functions/unified-apis.md): Build provider-specific functions behind one stable model and operation surface.
- [Platform: Observability](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/observability.md): How Tenklo helps you with observability for your integrations
- [Platform: Environments](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/environments.md): Organize your integrations & data with environments
- [Platform: Limits](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/limits.md): Overview of resource limits on Tenklo Cloud.
- [Platform: Security](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/security.md): How Tenklo secures your API credentials and customer data.
- [Platform: Audit trail](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/audit-trail.md): Review who changed what in your Tenklo account.
- [Platform: Proxy requests](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/proxy-requests.md): How to use the requests proxy from Tenklo
- [Platform: Receive webhooks from Tenklo](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/webhooks-from-nango.md): Reference for the webhooks Tenklo sends to your app — setup, types, payloads, signature verification, and retries.
- [Platform: External webhook forwarding](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/webhook-forwarding.md): Forward external API webhooks through Tenklo to your app, with connection attribution.
- [Platform: Common issues](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/common-issues.md): Troubleshooting guide for frequent errors and how to fix them.
- [Platform: Self-Hosting: Self-host Tenklo](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/self-hosting/self-hosting.md): Run Tenklo outside our cloud: BYOC or Self-Managed.
- [Platform: Self-Hosting: BYOC](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/self-hosting/byoc.md): Nango-managed, in your cloud.
- [Platform: Self-Hosting: Self-Managed](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/self-hosting/self-managed.md): You deploy, you operate.
- [Platform: Migrations: Migrate to checkpoints](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/migrations/migrate-to-checkpoints.md): Guide to migrate your sync functions from nango.lastSyncDate to the new checkpointing system.
- [Platform: Migrations: Migrate from end user](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/migrations/migrate-from-end-user.md): Guide to migrate away from using end users in connections and connect sessions
- [Platform: Migrations: Migrate from public key](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/migrations/migrate-from-public-key.md): Guide to migrate from using the public key (and HMAC) to a Connect session.
- [Platform: Migrations: Migrate from Connection MCP to agent sessions](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/migrations/migrate-from-connection-mcp.md): Replace the Connection MCP with a scoped agent session
- [Platform: Migrations: Migrating to Zero YAML](https://tenklo.dev/docs/guides/platform/migrations/migrate-to-zero-yaml.md): Guide on how to migrate to Zero YAML in Tenklo.
- [Platform: Contributing to Tenklo](https://tenklo.dev/docs/contributing.md): Learn which external contributions Tenklo reviews

## APIs and integrations

- [API catalog](https://tenklo.dev/docs/api-catalog.txt): 1072 provider slugs with canonical docs routes, auth modes, setup guides, and connect guides.
- Provider-specific pages are intentionally not expanded here so core Tenklo guides remain easy for agents to find.
